summary: Clarify composite rate-window behavior and configure separate burst pools for realtime vs batch pipelines
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated 429 responses for production realtime API traffic after migrating from per-route token windows to a composite (per-second + per-minute) window configuration. Impact: production latency and request failures for user-facing search autocompletion; intermittent errors affect ~12% of requests during peak spikes. Background: VectorSearch is on a dedicated pool with mixed workloads: low-latency autocomplete (short model calls) and bulk backfill embeddings. They recently applied a composite window policy intended to smooth bursts but observed more 429s for short-lived realtime sessions. They are asking for clarification on how the composite windows are applied and guidance on splitting burst pools for realtime vs batch to avoid cross-traffic exhaustion.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy configuration: enable composite token window (1s / 60s) on the tenant and make per-route weight 0.7 for realtime route and 0.3 for bulk route.
2) Start 200 concurrent short-lived websocket sessions (autocomplete) from a multihost orchestrator with rapid connect/disconnect (50 RPS sustained, microbursts to 400 RPS for 20s every 5 minutes).
3) Run a parallel bulk embed job that sends 8 large requests per second during the same timeframe.
4) Observe 429 responses on realtime route during microbursts and throttling headers indicating token window exhaustion.
observed_logs: 2026-03-09T17:02:14Z ingress-proxy[host-34] INFO 429 route=/v1/realtime reason=token_window_exhausted tenant=vecsearch window=(1s=120/120,60s=1500/2000)
2026-03-09T17:02:14Z rate-limiter DEBUG refill: tenant vecsearch composite: 1s_bucket full=false next_refill=0.54s
2026-03-09T17:02:15Z serving-runtime WARN request-id=cc3a short-circuit fallback to small-quant model due to concurrency limit
2026-03-09T17:05:00Z dedicated-pool INFO autoscaler scale_event desired_gpus=12 current_gpus=10 reason=cpu_hotspot
customer_notes: We applied the composite window to reduce microburst throttles but the opposite happened for our websocket-based autocomplete. The 429s started after switching configs and correlate with our periodic backfill windows.
We prefer to keep bulk embedding jobs running during business hours but need autocomplete to remain reliable for customers.
Can we allocate separate burst capacity or are we misunderstanding composite window accounting?
investigation_notes: Initial triage: 429s correspond to 1s bucket exhaustion even though 60s bucket shows remaining tokens — composite window logic enforces both buckets; exhaustion of any bucket triggers throttling.

Observed that ingress-proxy connection reuse (HTTP/2 multiplexing) and short-lived websocket reconnects cause rapid token consumption in the 1s window due to per-request preflight accounting. Healthcheck probes from orchestrator also contributed ~5% of 1s window usage during spikes.
Autoscaler events showed pool scaling lag (~90s) relative to microbursts, so capacity scaling did not assist 1s bucket exhaustion.

Hypothesis: per-route weight was not isolating burst credits as expected because tenant-level composite windows are applied before route weighting; route weights shift steady-state refill but do not prevent short-window cross-traffic exhaustion.
Test performed: created temporary separate route-level burst pool with dedicated burst credits (shadow mode) and observed 429s reduced by ~85% for realtime path during a replay of customer load.

resolution: Short-term: enabled route-level burst isolation (shadow mode) and exempted orchestrator healthchecks from per-request preflight accounting for 30-minute trial; immediate reduction in realtime 429s observed. Long-term recommendations: (1) Create separate burst pools for latency-sensitive realtime routes by configuring dedicated route burst credits or using a separate dedicated-pool node group; (2) keep composite windows if you want smoothing but bind per-route burst credits so the 1s bucket for realtime is not drained by bulk jobs; (3) tune autoscaler cooldown to 30s for dedicated pools handling mixed microbursts and set a small always-on headroom for realtime capacity; (4) avoid counting frequent healthcheck probes against token buckets (we will ship a config flag).
